notes: NCBI StatPearls Chondroblastoma was reread for adolescent/young-adult epiphyseal location, polygonal chondroblasts, osteoclast-type giant cells, chondroid material and chicken-wire calcification.
NCBI Holland-Frei bone-tumor chapter was reread for epiphyseal radiographic pattern and characteristic calcification.
PubMed clinicopathologic series was reread for second-decade predominance and frequent chicken-wire calcification.
The official USMLE 2026 Musculoskeletal domain was verified for bone neoplasms.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.location: Chondroblastoma classically arises in an epiphysis of a growing long bone in adolescents/young adults.
claim_audit.histology: Characteristic histology includes polygonal chondroblasts, osteoclast-type giant cells, chondroid matrix and fine pericellular chicken-wire calcification.
claim_audit.giant_cell_differential: Giant cell tumor typically occurs after physeal closure and shows diffuse giant cells in mononuclear stroma without characteristic chondroblastoma calcification.
claim_audit.osteoblastoma_differential: Osteoblastoma is an osteoid-producing lesion with woven bone rimmed by osteoblasts.
claim_audit.chondromyxoid_differential: Chondromyxoid fibroma more often arises eccentrically in metaphysis and shows lobulated myxoid/chondroid tissue.
claim_audit.osteosarcoma_differential: Osteosarcoma requires malignant osteoid production and cytologic malignancy.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A small well-circumscribed epiphyseal lytic lesion in a 16-year-old is a classic chondroblastoma setting. The histologic answer with chondroblasts, giant cells and chicken-wire calcification is uniquely characteristic.
adversarial_second_pass.giant_cell_tumor_challenge: Both can be epiphyseal and contain giant cells. Age/physeal context plus chicken-wire calcification and true chondroblasts distinguish chondroblastoma.
adversarial_second_pass.location_nuance: Chondroblastoma can occur in atypical locations and older adults, so epiphyseal adolescent location is a strong pattern rather than an absolute diagnostic rule.
adversarial_second_pass.h3f3b_nuance: H3F3B/H3.3 K36M is a useful modern molecular marker but is not required to answer this histology-focused item and avoids unnecessary molecular precision.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options are authentic bone-tumor histologies of similar specificity.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No lesion-size cutoff, mutation frequency, recurrence percentage or age threshold is required.
